turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm glad you came in today. What brings you in?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, yeah, thank you for seeing me. I, um... I'm here because I'm really struggling at work, and it's getting to the point where I'm genuinely terrified I'm going to get fired. I work at a meat processing plant—mostly doing processing and packing, but there's a lot of protocol involved. Like, a lot. And what brings me in is that I just... I keep messing up the procedures. Not the whole thing, but I'll start the sanitation steps, or I'll be filling out the batch logs, or doing the end-of-line paperwork, and I'll just somehow leave out the very last parts. 

And it's not like I don't know how to do it. I know exactly what needs to be done. I've got a bachelor's degree, you know? I'm not stupid. I know how important it is. In my line of work, if you don't finish the sanitation steps perfectly, it's a massive health hazard. The FDA could get involved, people could get sick. I know my job completely depends on finishing these things correctly, every single time. But I'll be scrubbing down the stations, going through the checklist in my head, and then I'll just... stop before the final rinse, or I'll fill out three pages of the batch log and completely forget to sign and date the bottom of the last page, or I'll just walk away from the end-of-line paperwork right before I'm supposed to file it. 

It's like my brain just decides "okay, we're done here" when we are very much not done. And my supervisor has been getting on me about it, and I try to explain, but what can I say? "Sorry I didn't finish the log, my brain just turned off"? It sounds like an excuse, but it really isn't. I just... I can't seem to follow through to the very end of anything, and it's ruining everything.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient describes making careless mistakes and missing details at work, such as forgetting to sign and date the bottom of a log or missing the final rinse.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient explicitly states they cannot follow through to the end of tasks and consistently fail to finish workplace duties like sanitation procedures and paperwork.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had trouble with attention or finishing tasks since childhood?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually. It's funny you ask that, because I was just talking to my mom about this the other day when I was panicking about work. She actually still has all my old report cards from elementary school—she's one of those moms who keeps absolutely everything in these huge plastic bins in the attic, you know? And she pulled out the ones from around, like, fourth grade, I think. And it's honestly kind of embarrassing to look at now, because every single teacher wrote the exact same thing. They all said I was bright, which, you know, is nice to hear, but then there was always a "but." It was always, "She's bright, but she needs constant reminders to finish her classwork," or "She needs to be reminded to turn in her homework." 

And the thing is, I remember doing the homework! I would sit at the kitchen table for hours, and I'd finish it, and then I'd just... leave it there. Or I'd put it in my folder and then never take it out of my folder when I got to school. It's just like what's happening at the plant now. And I remember sitting in class, and I would understand the lessons perfectly fine. Like, I wasn't struggling with the material at all. But when the teacher would give instructions for an assignment, it was like my brain would just tune out halfway through. I'd miss whole chunks of what we were supposed to do unless the teacher was literally standing right next to my desk, keeping me on track. If they walked away, I'd just sort of drift off or start doing something else, and then suddenly everyone is turning in their papers and I'm sitting there with half a worksheet done. So, yeah, it's definitely been happening for a really, really long time. It's just that back then, the consequence was a bad grade, and now the consequence is a massive health code violation and losing my job, which is just... a lot more terrifying.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes drifting off and leaving worksheets half-finished unless a teacher was present to keep them on track.
symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient notes that their brain would tune out halfway through when teachers were giving instructions.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient reports a childhood history of needing constant reminders to finish classwork and failing to turn in completed homework.
